headline: Sunny and mild through Sunday in Kentucky before late-night showers with a cold front and a sharp Monday cool-down; Upstate rain and gusty northeast wind today taper Sunday before a warm, dry Monday
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A surface ridge and dry southwest flow aloft keep Central Kentucky sunny and mild today. Return flow strengthens Sunday as an approaching northern-stream wave lowers heights and pushes a cold front toward the Ohio Valley. The front crosses Sunday night with only light rain because moisture is shallow, then cold advection and building high pressure bring a much cooler Monday and a near-freezing Monday night.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 7:54 AM EST, KDVK reported 32°F with a 30°F dew point, calm wind, clear sky and visibility above 10 miles. At 7:55 AM, KLEX reported 42°F with a 31°F dew point, southeast wind near 5 mph and clear sky. No official NWS point alert was active for Danville at the final issuance check.

days.label: Saturday / Saturday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. No widespread hazardous weather is expected. The independent concern is a large rural temperature spread tonight; widespread fog, rain and a widespread freeze are not expected.
days.forecast: Sunny and unusually mild after the cold valley start, with a most-likely Danville high near 69°F. Southeast to south wind remains light at 3–7 mph. Mostly clear conditions continue tonight before some high cloud arrives late. The most-likely Sunday-morning low is near 44°F, with colder sheltered valleys several degrees lower.

days.label: Sunday / Sunday night
days.precipitation: 5% or less through afternoon; 55–70% evening and overnight
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Sunday at issuance. Independent concerns are gusty showers and a wind shift with the cold front Sunday evening and night. Rainfall should remain light—generally a few hundredths of an inch—and flooding, severe thunderstorms and hazardous wind are not expected.
days.forecast: Most of Sunday stays dry and mild. Sunshine becomes filtered by increasing clouds, with a most-likely high near 68°F and south to southwest wind around 4–9 mph. A weakening band of showers reaches the Danville area mainly from about 7 PM–3 AM EST, plus or minus three hours. Gusts around 15–25 mph are possible near the front before rain tapers toward Monday morning. The most-likely overnight low is near 46°F.

days.label: Monday / Monday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Monday at issuance. Independent concern shifts to a likely freeze in colder valleys Monday night and a possible freeze near Danville by early Tuesday. Any early shower is brief and light; no flooding or thunder is expected.
days.forecast: A leftover shower is possible very early, then clouds break as much colder and drier air arrives on north wind around 6–10 mph with gusts of 15–20 mph. The most-likely high is near 53°F, occurring before temperatures level off or slowly fall. Monday night turns clear and cold, with a most-likely low near 30°F and a freeze likely in sheltered locations by early Tuesday.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky is sunny and near 70°F today and again Sunday. Most-likely Danville high/low pairs are 69/44°F, 68/46°F and 53/30°F. A light, briefly gusty shower band crosses mainly Sunday evening and night, followed by a sharp Monday cool-down and a likely freeze in colder valleys Monday night.
kentucky.confidence: High today; high in Sunday's daytime temperatures and moderate-high in the Sunday-night shower timing; high in Monday's cool-down but moderate in the exact Monday-night minimum

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: A cool, stable northeast flow is feeding a shallow cold-air wedge while a moist southern disturbance lifts toward the Carolinas. Isentropic ascent above that cool layer spreads rain into Clemson and Central this afternoon and tonight, accompanied by gusty northeast wind and lowering ceilings. The disturbance exits Sunday and the wedge gradually erodes, but lingering rain, low cloud and fog make the speed of warming uncertain. A drier west-flow regime supports sunshine and a strong rebound Monday.
upstate.currentConditions: From 7:53–7:56 AM EST, KCEU reported 56°F with a 29°F dew point and northeast wind near 9 mph beneath broken cloud near 3,600 feet; KLQK reported 57°F with a 25°F dew point and northeast wind near 6 mph; KGSP was 55°F with a 30°F dew point and north-northeast wind near 13 mph beneath a broken ceiling near 2,900 feet; KAND was 58°F with a 31°F dew point. No official NWS point alert was active. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Saturday / Saturday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. Independent concerns are wet roads, northeast gusts around 25–32 mph, lowering ceilings and patchy fog tonight. Flooding, severe thunderstorms and ice are not expected.
days.forecast: Cloudy, cool and increasingly windy, with a most-likely corridor high near 61°F. Rain develops south to north during the afternoon and becomes steadier this evening and overnight. Northeast wind runs 10–16 mph with gusts around 25–32 mph. Rainfall of roughly 0.20–0.50 inch is expected. The most-likely Sunday-morning low is near 54°F, with local station differences inside the calibrated range.

days.label: Sunday / Sunday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Sunday at issuance. Independent concerns are morning wet roads and low ceilings, plus conditional patchy or locally dense valley fog redeveloping late Sunday night if clearing occurs and wind weakens. The main forecast uncertainty is how quickly the shallow wedge and stratus erode; thunder, flooding and hazardous wind are not expected.
days.forecast: Morning rain tapers, but low cloud and patchy fog may linger for several hours. Gradual afternoon improvement follows with lighter north to northeast wind. The most-likely high is near 65°F; a stubborn wedge could hold temperatures near 60–62°F, while earlier breaks of sun would support the upper 60s. The most-likely overnight low is near 50°F. Partial clearing and light wind may allow valley fog to redevelop late Sunday night into early Monday.

days.label: Monday / Monday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Monday at issuance. Conditional patchy or locally dense valley fog is possible early if clearing occurs and wind weakens; after it dissipates, no independent hazardous-weather signal is present. A mostly dry cold front approaches Monday night, with cooler air arriving near or after the 72-hour endpoint.
days.forecast: Patchy valley fog may briefly reduce visibility early, then mostly sunny, dry and unseasonably warm conditions develop after the wedge fully erodes, with a most-likely corridor high near 72°F. West to southwest wind remains light at 2–7 mph. Clouds increase late Monday night ahead of a dry front, with a most-likely low near 51°F and temperatures near 49–53°F at the early-Tuesday 72-hour endpoint.

upstate.bottomLine: Rain develops this afternoon and continues tonight with gusty northeast wind, low ceilings and roughly 0.20–0.50 inch expected. Most-likely corridor high/low pairs are 61/54°F, 65/50°F and 72/51°F. Rain tapers Sunday morning, but the exact high depends on wedge erosion. Monday is dry, sunny and much warmer. Tempest data remains excluded.
upstate.confidence: Moderate-high today; moderate Sunday because guidance sharply disagrees on the speed of wedge and stratus erosion; high Monday

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERTS: no active NWS point alert was present for Danville, Clemson or Central at the final issuance check. Official alerts remain separate from outlooks and this independent analysis.

The Louisville discussion supports a mild and dry weekend, light rain with a Sunday-evening or Sunday-night frontal passage, only a couple hundredths across much of the Bluegrass, and a colder Monday and Tuesday. Gusts may briefly reach 15–20 mph, with an isolated higher gust near the front.

Chris Bailey's November 21 Kentucky Weather Center post, ‘A Sunday Night Cold Front Starts a Big Change,’ was accepted as authoritative published source material. Bailey forecasts a sunny, mild Saturday, 65–70°F Sunday with gusty showers Sunday night, and much colder air arriving late Monday and Monday night. Details absent from his post or unreadable in graphics were left unknown.

The Greenville-Spartanburg discussion supports increased Upstate rainfall of roughly 0.10–0.50 inch, rain today and tonight into early Sunday, overnight IFR ceilings, gradual Sunday improvement, and Monday as the warmest day of the next week.

The Sunday Upstate temperature spread is material but resolvable: GFS retains fog and stratus and holds highs near the upper 50s, while RRFS warms Clemson toward the upper 60s. The 62–67°F calibrated range, most-likely value near 65°F and moderate confidence explicitly represent uncertainty in wedge and stratus erosion.

Official point guidance supports Danville near 68/43°F, 67/46°F and 55/30°F, and Clemson near 61/52°F, 68/48°F and 73/51°F. Independent calibrated ranges incorporate station corrections and model spread rather than copying the point values.

COD radar at 13:00Z showed Central Kentucky dry while precipitation covered parts of the Southeast and advanced north toward the Upstate. GOES-19 infrared imagery at 12:56Z showed a broad Southeast cloud shield with clearer conditions over Kentucky, supporting today's regional contrast.

Every currently available COD family was audited at 13:04Z: HRRR, RAP, RRFS, GEM-RDPS, GEM-GDPS, ECMWF, GFS, AIFS, AIGFS, CFSv2, GEFS, REFS, AIFS-ENS and AIGEFS. NAM, NAM Nest, SREF and HiResW are retired; retained files were stale and excluded.

Fresh local BUFKIT 19 GFS, HRRR, RAP and RRFS profiles were consulted. They sharpened the Upstate rain, northeast-wind, low-ceiling and fog risks; the strongest fog signal is conditional on clearing and light wind late Sunday night into Monday morning. Local raw GRIB files that were stale were excluded.
The maintained KDVK −1.5°F low correction and Kentucky empirical 5/5/6°F high and 8°F low widths were applied. Prose supplies one most-likely Danville value inside each calibrated range.
The maintained KCEU +1.5°F and KLQK −3.5°F low corrections preserve the Clemson–Central nighttime split inside current 10°F regional low ranges. Upstate high widths remain 4/5/6°F.
The latest completed accuracy summary contains 155 verified checkpoints across 54 forecasts and all-category accuracy of 81.3% overall, including 84.8% for Central Kentucky and 77.7% for the Upstate.
Current station corrections, empirical lead-specific widths, model records, calibrated confidence, explicit event windows, fog timing and official-alert separation were applied.
All local times use Eastern Standard Time. The third card includes Monday night and early Tuesday because validThrough is exactly 72 elapsed hours after issuance.
Contains modified ECMWF Open Data, selected and processed for independent forecast research under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
This is a candidate only. No repository, forecast history, website, widget or publishing workflow was modified during preparation.
